body:
## Problem

On Linux, a failed child signal-mask restore or stdin/stdout redirection returned `EXIT_FAILURE` through a Boolean launcher. That could send the failed fork child back into controller execution and permit unintended worker creation.

## What changes

Terminate those three fatal setup paths with `_exit(EXIT_FAILURE)`. Add 14 CPU-only subprocess regressions covering each failure during first-slot, last-slot and recovery launches, plus healthy replay/recovery, parent death and adjacent fatal checks.

## Why this matters

A failed setup child must terminate while its original controller retains ownership and reaps it. The tests assert exact exits, process births, reaping, protocol-pipe closure and absence of survivors.

## Why this approach

Direct `_exit` matches the neighboring fatal setup branches and avoids inherited cleanup callbacks and buffered stdio flushing. Fault injection is confined to the test executable. Public interfaces, shared layouts and normal replay behavior are unchanged.

## Verification and limits

Fresh unit and separate final checkers each passed all 105 CTests in Linux Debug and Release with exceptions disabled and enabled. All 14 lifecycle scenarios passed three repeated executions per checker. Each of the three original-header defects failed the intended fallthrough/exit-status assertions; healthy and healthy-recovery controls passed. All four full builds passed for each role.

Windows verification was explicitly skipped at the user's request. Null-device replay does not establish real GPU, Steam or driver-cache behavior. The existing aggregate controller-success policy for a worker lost before progress is preserved; retained-loss/result reporting belongs to separate issues.

## Task references

Closes https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/56

The parent lifecycle epic https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/46 remains open.
